question.prompt: Each of 2 people rolls a die. Player A wins if the sum of the numbers rolled is even, and Player B wins if it is odd. Is the game fair? (Give the probabilities of Player A and Player B winning, in that order, as fractions in simplest form, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes in total. An even sum requires both numbers to have the same parity, giving 18 outcomes. There are also 18 outcomes with an odd sum. The probabilities of Player A and Player B winning are both \(1/2\), so the game is fair.
solutions.title: Count outcomes by parity
